description: Runtime context-injection is fragmented across overlapping surfaces with an undocumented division of labor and a duplicated, drift-prone source, which confuses the agent runtime about what is authoritative and where to get context. The surfaces: (1) SessionStart hook `.factory/hooks/loop-surface-inject.cjs` — push, cold, automatic at startup; per its header (:3) it claims to "inject loop_describe({tier:summary}) into context" but actually renders hardcoded LOCAL_DISCOVERABILITY_HINTS + LOCAL_PROCESS_HINTS copies plus a separately-spawned registry summary (the MCP server is spawned for counts but its hint strings are NOT trusted — security comment :14-16: "The server's discoverability_hints field is not trusted at render time. To update the hints, edit this file and commit"). (2) `loop_describe` MCP tool (loop-describe-tool.js) — pull, on-demand, tiered hot/warm/cold/summary; returns the CANONICAL buildDiscoverabilityHints()+buildProcessHints() (core/loop-introspect.js) PLUS dynamic `rules`/`tools`/`active_findings`/`loop_designs` read live from the registry. (3) `loop_get_instruction` MCP tool — pull, on-demand single-hint lookup by slug/index. (4) AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / `learning-loop` skill — static always-loaded steering prompt + prompt-author docs. Overlaps that confuse the runtime: (a) the SAME hints are delivered via two channels (push at SessionStart from a LOCAL copy, pull via loop_describe from the CANONICAL copy) with a parity test (cold-session-discoverability) enforcing they match — neither is "the" source, and editing one without the other drifts (this just caused a CI failure: rule promoted, canonical PROCESS_HINTS row added, LOCAL mirror missed). (b) Within loop_describe itself an agent-checklist rule appears in BOTH the dynamic `rules` field AND a hand-curated `process_hints` row; the H6 gate (loop-describe-tool.js:111-118) couples them by nagging "Add a hint referencing this rule to core/loop-introspect.js PROCESS_HINTS" rather than auto-generating — so one rule is represented in the registry entry, the dynamic rules field, a canonical hint row, a LOCAL hook hint row, and possibly AGENTS.md. (c) The stated principle (canonical/hook hint: "Each surface has a distinct role; do not duplicate content across them") is violated by design: the hook↔canonical hint duplication and the rule↔process_hints coupling ARE cross-surface duplication, kept because the hook deliberately mistrusts server hint strings at render time. (d) No documented division of labor between push (SessionStart) and pull (loop_describe / loop_get_instruction): an agent that already has the SessionStart hints does not know whether calling loop_describe warm tier adds anything (it does — dynamic rules/findings — but the hints block is the same content), and loop_get_instruction re-lookup of a hint already in the SessionStart injection is redundant. Recommendation: document the surface division of labor (push=cold-start fixed context, pull=current/deep context, on-demand=single re-fetch); make the trust boundary explicit and single-source the hints the hook DOES trust (e.g., the hook reads canonical via a node helper that imports the ESM core, or auto-generates process_hints rows for agent-checklist rules so promotion is one tool call not three); and reconcile the "do not duplicate across surfaces" principle with the hook's security-driven LOCAL copy (either trust the canonical at render with a signature/integrity check, or accept the duplication but make it mechanically enforced, not parity-tested). Related but distinct from meta-260715T2237Z-entry-relationships (that finding is about entry cross-ref storage/validation/retrieval; this is about the runtime context-INJECTION surfaces that deliver those entries to the agent).
resolution: Resolved by plans/260717-1826-unify-context-injection (Phase 1-4, completed 2026-07-17). Change-log: meta-260717T2006Z. Fixes: (a) LOCAL_* hint mirror deleted — factory hook renders canonical builders via direct core import; (b) MCP spawn probe killed — counts come from cheap core readers; (c) H6 ordering-gate nag deleted — rule-derived hint_text projection enforced at promotion time; (d) division of labor documented in docs/architecture.md § Context-Injection Division of Labor (push / pull-warm / pull-single / static); trust boundary explicit (hooks read core directly, no server-rendered strings cross trust). State-2 mechanism preserved (deterministic injection, agentic consumption).

description: runtime_state_record's `metadata` param (z.record(z.unknown())) accepts arbitrarily nested values, but array-typed values inside metadata were corrupted in transit on the npx-skills-mastra-roundtrip-2026-07-19 ledger row: pending_execution landed as 7-deep nested arrays containing a stray closing-tag artifact, and the row's fingerprint was computed over the corrupt payload. runtime-state.jsonl is append-only, so there is no in-place repair path — the corrected row had to be appended as a superseding entry (fingerprint sha256:0abcf89...). description: Central-skills Phase 3 chose a runtime-state ledger-event hand-off as the Q4 npx-unavailable fallback: "whichever sandbox can run npx executes the round-trip, writes a ledger-event, and Phase 3 reads it back to confirm." Three coupled failures: (a) no sandbox is constructed or selected — a static plan cannot pick which executor runs npx; (b) the report-back loop is untested — no test asserts the round-trip criterion flips on a row; (c) the same-id "correction" append at runtime-state.jsonl:24 cannot supersede the 08:13:00 row at any id-keyed `find` site, because findDispatchRow (tools/learning-loop-mastra/tools/handlers/meta-state-dispatch-finding-tool.js:45-50) returns the first match. The schema at schemas/runtime-state.schema.json:15-18 defines id as ^[a-z0-9-]+$ only — no uniqueness, no supersession field; same-id append-correction masquerades as supersession via metadata.supersedes_fingerprint but no read site honors it. This is the escape-hatch-abuse subtype: the writer's "I corrected it" assumption collides with the reader's first-match-wins. The inversion: a static plan cannot "read runtime-state back and mark a criterion met" — only a test does. Resolution: drop the hand-off from plans/260719-1428-central-skills-management Phase 3; gate the npx-round-trip criterion on the F6 hash test (phase-03 step 17: real npx when available; hash-recompute-and-compare when not); decouple F11/F12 from the ledger row to plain presence + byte-identity tests; strike the two corrupt same-id rows from runtime-state.jsonl. See plan 260720-1404.

npx skills CLI clobbers skills-lock.json on every `npx skills add`/`update`, rewriting the mastra entry to its native format (sourceType:"github", computedHash) and dropping the extended trust-anchor fields (external:true, delivery, targets, maturity, hash). The contract's manifest-driven exclusion (contract.js listLoopMaintainedSkills) reads external:true to exclude mastra; with the field dropped, mastra is enumerated and the F10 parity test fails. Verified empirically 2026-07-20: `npx skills add mastra-ai/skills --copy` and `npx skills update mastra` both clobbered the manifest. Workaround: after every npx add/update, restore the extended mastra entry (hash = sha256 of the detected SKILL.md) then `pnpm skills:sync`. A self-healing `pnpm skills:normalize` step is the sustainable fix (tracked follow-up).

description: Transport diversification to a CLI is a deferred decision, now gated on three triggers (T1/T2/T3). The loop realizes the runtime-contract (docs/runtime-contract.md) via a single transport — MCP+hooks, wired for 3 runtimes; shell-hook-only and library-import are named but unwired. Per plans/reports/from-root-cause-to-transport-decision-260711-0011-mcp-stateless-adapter-vs-cli-report.md, the CLI swap (Option C) was deferred under two triggers: T1 chronic lifecycle pain (stale-PID kills, not a one-off 22h server); T2 acceptable ergonomics loss (agent tolerates Bash-as-tool-channel, no zod, bash-gate allowlisting the loop's own CLI). A 2026-07-21 ak:predict session (standpoint: plan 260720-1955 context-size + delivery-observability) added a third trigger on a new axis: T3 chronic silent-undelivery of push-steering that a pull-based CLI would structurally prevent — distinct from T1/T2's statefulness axis. T3 is only measurable once plan 260720-1955 ships its delivery classifier (delivery-<sessionId> rows in runtime-state.jsonl); until then T3 is opinion (same shape as 260711-0011 Unresolved Q1). No CLI wiring until at least one trigger fires with evidence. Contract clarification (shell-hook-only = read-only) is recorded on meta-260711T0125Z; this finding tracks the wiring gate. Ship plan 260720-1955 first; re-evaluate T3 against classifier data post-plan.

docs/runtime-contract.md has a transport-agnostic contract gap between Capability 3 (record routing) and the shell-hook-only transport description. Capability 3 states: "The runtime never writes `records/**`, `meta-state.jsonl`, or `runtime-state.jsonl` directly. All writes go through the loop's tools, so the registry's invariants (4-kind union, status lifecycle, grounding fingerprints) hold regardless of which runtime produced the record." The shell-hook-only transport description states: "only the gate hooks are wired (no MCP tool surface); the runtime relies on the loop's file-based records **without a tool channel**." These two statements tension: if there is no tool channel, how do writes satisfy Capability 3? Two readings surfaced in plans/reports/from-root-cause-to-transport-decision-260711-0011-mcp-stateless-adapter-vs-cli-report.md §7: (a) shell-hook-only is read-only participation (capability 3 is unsatisfiable under that transport, contract should say so); (b) a CLI counts as a tool channel (just not MCP), so the contract should name it and wiring a CLI would *define* the shell-hook-only transport rather than merely wire it. Unresolved since plan 260711-0011 (Unresolved Question #2 in the prior decision report). This is a pre-existing L2 design question; the current plan 260711-0030 (stateless MCP adapter) does NOT wire shell-hook-only and explicitly defers the question. Decision needed before any non-MCP transport is wired (library-import or CLI). Deferred to follow-up plan per the prior report's recommendation. Scope: contract clarification + optional transport definition.

**Consensus (2026-07-21 ak:predict session):** adopt reading (a) — shell-hook-only is **read-only participation**; Capability 3 is unsatisfiable under that transport and the contract should state so. A CLI would *define* a write-capable tool channel (non-MCP), named as a future option, not wired now. Resolution is **docs-only**: update `docs/runtime-contract.md` Capability 3 + transport mapping so shell-hook-only carries no write path, and a CLI (if ever wired) is the minimal write-capable tool channel. No transport wiring in this resolution. The CLI-swap *wiring* decision is tracked separately in `meta-260721T0809Z-transport-diversification-to-a-cli-is-a-deferred-decision-no` under a three-trigger gate (T1 chronic lifecycle pain; T2 acceptable ergonomics loss; T3 chronic silent-undelivery a pull-CLI structurally prevents; plan 260720-1955's delivery classifier instruments T3). This finding resolves when the docs clarification commits.

SessionStart steering injection is push-dependent and silently undelivered on lean provider profiles; transcript records injections that never reach the model (transcript ≠ wire). Measured: session b96b96c3-0808-4a40-8a2b-466b84a50975 (GLM-5.2 via CCS syn profile with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1) recorded ~101KB of SessionStart/listing attachments but its first API call totalled 9,322 tokens with zero hint visibility (no hint references in thinking, no loop_describe call); same harness+hooks on the mm profile delivered a 67,890-token first call (session 7b63f076-b35d-4d53-9d1d-2732d78bbe39). Enforcement is delivery-independent and survived (hooks execute harness-side; gates need no prompt channel; MCP tool contracts re-deliver at invocation) — graceful degradation, task completed correctly. What degrades is state-1 steering (discovery rituals, process hints, canonical-tool preferences) with no error signal: (a) citizenship drift across profiles; (b) measurement corruption — "model ignored hint" vs "hint never sent" are behaviorally indistinguishable, so cross-profile compliance metrics are unsound without delivery tagging; (c) profile switches are user-initiated and invisible to the loop. Related but distinct locus: meta-260704T0959Z-orchestrator-session-read-the-full-326-line-source-of-tools (per-call behavioral unreliability of prose channels; this finding is per-session structural delivery — neither subsumes the other). Remediation direction (plans/reports/debug-260719-1524-ak-cook-context-attribution.md §Addendum 2): pointer-not-payload steering via UserPromptSubmit hook (verified survivor on the lean path), payloads pull-based (loop_describe / .claude/session-context.json), per-profile delivery attestation via one wire capture, session tagging by active profile. Exact strip point (harness flag vs synthetic.new proxy transform) unverified without a wire capture.
resolution: Remediation realized in plan 260720-1955: SessionStart steering is delivered as a pull pointer (slug — suggestion projection, combined hook stdout 13,088 → 5,120 chars) plus a once-per-session inbound-gate pull pointer (V2, suppress-token-gated), not a silent push. Delivery is now observable: tools/scripts/delivery-classify.mjs writes delivery-<sessionId> ledger rows (full/lean/unknown, content-hash re-classify V5) to runtime-state.jsonl, queryable via runtime_state_read; delivered-token metric = input + cache_read + cache_creation (H7). Pull payloads intact (sidecar shape hash unchanged, *_source=core). Manifest-tool wire slimmed to 39,905 B (≤40 kB) via JIT branch contracts + shared field glossary. Verification: plans/260720-1955-.../reports/verification-260720-final.md. syn-profile forensics recorded as documented-degradation (transcript absent).

Agent runtime embeds plan IDs, phase numbers, and finding codes in stable code artifacts (code comments, test names, migration names, commit messages) despite the operator's global rule `review-audit-self-decision.md` § "Stable Code Artifacts" forbidding exactly that ("Do not put plan IDs, phase numbers, audit labels, or finding codes in code comments, migration names, test names, or commit messages. Explain the invariant or behavior directly.").

Self-reinforcing: an established codebase convention PRECEDES the rule (~42 instances across core/ + mastra/ — bound-artifacts.js:5/93, hint-renderer.js:3, surfaces.js:50/69/126, evaluate-write-gate.js:92/96/100/185, gate-logic.js:35, check-grounding.js:23/35, path-containment.js:30, inbound-state.js:9, file-readers.js:10, placement.yaml rows 19/22/46/77/86), and the development-rules baseline "match surrounding code" causes every new feature to propagate it. Most recent recurrence: the CLI-transport phase-1 slice (bin/loop.mjs:2, core/schema-normalize.js:8, mastra/create-loop-tool.js:18, core/placement.yaml:86, all 3 new test-file headers) embeds "Phase N of plan 260721-1933" — 7 instances.

Harm: plan IDs are ephemeral lineage; code comments are stable artifacts. Embedding them couples stable code to transient process state — plan dirs get archived/renamed, leaving dangling references that fail no test. It also contradicts an explicit operator rule, eroding rule credibility.

Alternative commenting convention: describe the INVARIANT or BEHAVIOR directly, not plan lineage. If a cross-reference is needed, link by concept/topic (e.g. "see docs/runtime-contract.md § Transport mapping") not by plan ID. Put plan lineage in plan docs, cook reports, and git history — never in code.

Prevention: (a) promote an agent-checklist rule restating the operator's "Stable Code Artifacts" rule so agent runtimes see it at session start; (b) add a regression test that greps core/+mastra/+bin/ source for plan-ID comment patterns and fails on NEW matches — but it MUST exclude legitimate test-fixture usages (plan paths used as test INPUT data or evidence_journal fixture values, e.g. evaluate-write-gate.test.js:259, meta-state-g8-supersede.test.js:43) and docs (README.md). Comprehensive removal is a separate hand-edit sweep (rewrite each comment to describe the invariant), NOT a mechanical find-replace.

title: Plan-ID-free stable code artifacts — removal sweep, alternative convention, prevention test
description:
Resolve finding meta-260721T2300Z-agent-runtime-embeds-plan-ids-phase-numbers-and-finding-code in three coordinated steps.

STEP 1 — Alternative convention (codify first so the sweep has a target): code comments describe the invariant/behavior directly; cross-references link by concept (docs/ section or module name), never by plan ID/phase number/finding code. Plan lineage lives in plan docs, cook reports, and git history only. Add this to docs/code-standards.md as the "Stable code artifacts" section, quoting the operator's global rule verbatim.

STEP 2 — Comprehensive removal sweep (hand-edit, NOT mechanical find-replace): for each of the ~42 established + 7 new instances, rewrite the comment to describe the invariant. Examples: `// Phase 3 of plans/260707-0114-loop-skill-layer-prerequisite/plan.md.` → `// Bound-artifact registry: the trust root for which generated files the gate may touch.`; `// removed by migration in plan 260607-dual-field-schema-unification` → `// Legacy dual-field shape is no longer produced; the single canonical field is ...`. Each rewrite requires reading the surrounding code to name the actual invariant. DO NOT touch legitimate test-fixture usages (plan paths as test INPUT data or evidence_journal fixture values — evaluate-write-gate.test.js:259, meta-state-g8-supersede.test.js:43) or docs (README.md).

STEP 3 — Prevention regression test: add __tests__/stable-artifacts-no-plan-ids.test.js that greps core/+mastra/+bin/ source (excluding __tests__ fixture lines and .md docs) for plan-ID comment patterns — /\b(plan|plans)\/\d{6}-/, /Phase \d+ of (plan|plans)/, /plan \d{6}-\d{4}/ — and fails on any match. Seed it with a snapshot of the CURRENT matched lines as the allowlist baseline (so the sweep removes entries incrementally and the test locks the floor: no NEW matches). Once the sweep completes, the allowlist is empty and the test forbids all plan-ID comments. This is the regression that prevents agent runtime recurrence.

Rollback: each step is independently revertible; the test is additive; the sweep is comment-only (no behavior change).

Idempotent: re-running the sweep is a no-op once the allowlist is empty.

description:
Promoting an agent-checklist rule is a manual 4-location cascade with no automated coupling, and 3 of those locations hardcode registry counts that are trivially derivable. This just caused the PR-#73 CI failure (rule-no-plan-ids-in-stable-code-artifacts).

The 4 locations an agent-checklist rule promotion MUST touch:
1. `meta-state.jsonl` — the rule entry (id, enforcement, pattern_type=agent-checklist, pattern, hint_text). Done by `meta_state_promote_rule` MCP tool. This is the ONLY location the tool writes.
2. `core/hint-registry.js` — a hand-mirrored `HINT_REGISTRY` entry with `derived_from_rule === rule.id`, a slug, `kind: "process"`, `text: ""` (renderer resolves prose from `rule.hint_text`), and a one-line `suggestion`. The promote tool CANNOT write this (it writes the registry, not source code). Missing it fails `legacy-mcp/consult-checklist-process-hints-coverage.test.js` (the Phase-3 invariant: every active agent-checklist rule MUST have a matching `derived_from_rule` registry entry). This is the failure that broke CI.
3. `__tests__/hint-registry.test.cjs` — hardcodes `process` slug count (10), `buildProcessHints` length (10), `listHints({kind:'process'})` length (10), and total (26).
4. `__tests__/hint-renderer.test.cjs` + `__tests__/rule-derived-process-hints.test.cjs` — hardcode total hints (26), degraded-skip warnings count (8), sidecar `process_hints` length (10), mcp-warm array length (26), provenance rows (26), and "8 rule-derived process rows at positions 2-10".

Root smell: the numeric counts (26/10/8) are PURE DERIVATIONS of `HINT_REGISTRY.length`, `.filter(e => e.derived_from_rule).length`, and `.filter(e => e.kind === 'process').length` — yet they are hand-locked as literals. Adding one rule-derived hint bumps 26->27, 10->11, 8->9 and requires hand-editing all 3 test files. The agent must know to do this; nothing enforces or reminds them. The slug-list + ordering assertions in these tests ARE legitimate (they catch real drift) and should stay hardcoded — only the pure-numeric counts should be derived.

Two coupled gaps:
A. The promote tool does not (cannot) create the companion `HINT_REGISTRY` entry — the agent must hand-edit `core/hint-registry.js`. No reminder, no checklist hint (ironically, the rule-promotion workflow itself lacks the agent-checklist treatment).
B. The count-locking tests hardcode derivable numbers, turning a 1-location registry addition into a 4-file manual cascade.

Remediation direction:
- Gap A: either (i) a companion `register_hint_for_rule` MCP tool (or a `meta_state_promote_rule` option) that appends the `HINT_REGISTRY` entry to `core/hint-registry.js` from the rule id + hint_text (slug = rule-id minus 'rule-' prefix; suggestion = first sentence of hint_text; derived_from_rule = rule.id), so promotion is 1 MCP call; or (ii) an agent-checklist rule + regression test that forbids an active agent-checklist rule without a `HINT_REGISTRY` entry (the coverage test already does this — so the real fix is making the promote path produce the entry, not just flag its absence).
- Gap B: replace the hardcoded numeric counts in the 3 test files with `HINT_REGISTRY`-derived values (`registry.HINT_REGISTRY.length`, `.filter(derived_from_rule).length`, `.filter(kind==='process').length`). Keep the slug-list + ordering + per-partition-budget assertions hardcoded (those are the real signal). After this, adding a rule-derived hint is: 1 promote call + 1 slug-list append (the legitimate drift signal) — not a 4-file cascade.

Evidence: the PR-#73 CI failure (run 29849986465, `test` workflow) was exactly gap A (missing HINT_REGISTRY entry); the 9 follow-on test failures from the fix were exactly gap B (hardcoded counts). Both gaps are reproducible by promoting any new agent-checklist rule.

title: Single-location agent-checklist rule promotion — derive hint-registry counts, auto-register the hint entry
description:
Close the two coupled gaps from meta-260722T0001Z so promoting an agent-checklist rule is a 1-location change (the rule) + at most 1 slug-list append (the legitimate drift signal), not a 4-file manual cascade.

STEP 1 — Derive the count locks (Gap B). In the 3 count-locking test files, replace hardcoded numeric counts with HINT_REGISTRY-derived values:
- `hint-registry.test.cjs`: `proc.length` and `listHints({kind:'process'}).length` -> `registry.HINT_REGISTRY.filter(e => e.kind === 'process').length`; `listHints({kind:undefined}).length` -> `registry.HINT_REGISTRY.length`; `buildProcessHints` length -> same process count. KEEP the slug-list `deepStrictEqual` (legitimate drift signal) and the standalone-rows-position assertions.
- `hint-renderer.test.cjs`: `provenance.length` / `slugs.size` / mcp-warm `arr.length` -> `registry.HINT_REGISTRY.length` (27 today, derived); degraded-skip `warnings.length` -> `registry.HINT_REGISTRY.filter(e => e.derived_from_rule).length`; sidecar `process_hints.length` -> process count. KEEP per-partition budget + 2-partition-shape + slug/marker presence assertions.
- `rule-derived-process-hints.test.cjs`: `derived.length` -> `.filter(derived_from_rule).length`; KEEP the standalone-position assertions (0 and 8) and `standalone.length === 2` (the 2 standalone rows are a real invariant, not a derivation of the rule count).
After this step, adding a rule-derived hint changes ONLY the slug-list expected array in `hint-registry.test.cjs` (the real signal that a new slug landed in the right place) — the numeric tests auto-track the registry.

STEP 2 — Auto-register the hint entry on promotion (Gap A). Add a companion code-writing step to the agent-checklist promotion path. Two viable shapes (pick in plan):
- (i) `meta_state_promote_rule` gains a `register_hint: true` default for agent-checklist that appends the `HINT_REGISTRY` entry to `core/hint-registry.js` from the rule: slug = rule_id without `rule-` prefix; kind = 'process'; text = '' (renderer resolves from hint_text); suggestion = first sentence of hint_text (<= ~160 chars); derived_from_rule = rule_id. The tool already writes meta-state.jsonl; extending it to also edit the one source file is the single-point fix. Gate the source edit through the existing write-gate (`core/hint-registry.js` is loop-source, not a preflight-gated path, so it's writable).
- (ii) A standalone `register_hint_for_rule` MCP tool the agent calls right after promote, taking rule_id + optional slug/suggestion override. Lower-risk (no change to promote semantics) but 2 calls instead of 1.

Add a test that promotes a throwaway agent-checklist rule in a tmpdir registry + tmpdir hint-registry copy and asserts the hint entry was created with `derived_from_rule === rule.id` (locks step 2's behavior). Plus, after step 1, add a test that asserts NONE of the 3 count-locking test files contain a bare numeric literal for the registry size (grep guard: `/\b===?\s*(26|10|8|27|11|9)\b/` in those files' count assertions -> fail), so a future edit can't silently re-hardcode the counts.

Idempotent: once step 1 lands, re-deriving counts is a no-op; once step 2 lands, re-promoting an already-promoted rule is a no-op (hint entry already exists).

runtime-state.jsonl has two coupled maintenance gaps that let stale/non-actionable rows accumulate and pollute the loop's own ledger view. Surfaced by the inbound gate reporting 15 stale vnstock runtime-state observations alongside 12 meta-state-tools ones — vnstock is a vendored example surface in this template, not a system the operator is running, yet its ledger-events persist and crowd out the loop's own records.

GAP 1 — no versioned dedup (unlike meta-state). meta-state.jsonl is versioned-append: each id can have multiple version lines and reads collapse by max_by(version) (meta_state_list's projection). runtime-state.jsonl has NO version field: the row schema is {affected_system, kind, id, source_ref, value, delta, timestamp, metadata, fingerprint} where `fingerprint` is a SHA-256 row-INTEGRITY hash (detects post-write mutation), NOT an idempotency/version key. `appendLedgerEvent` (core/runtime-state.js) ALWAYS appends; `readRuntimeStateRows` returns every row; `runtime_state_read` filters then `.slice(0, limit=20)` with no per-id max-by-version projection. Re-recording the same ledger-event `id` (e.g. a budget-state row for the same source_ref, or a re-dispatch) creates duplicate rows, and reads return up to 20 stale copies of the same logical event. Evidence: core/runtime-state.js readRuntimeStateRows + appendLedgerEvent + the runtime-state-read handler's filter-then-slice (no version/dedup). Fix direction: add a `version` field to runtime-state rows (or reuse id+source_ref as the dedup key) and have `runtime_state_read` collapse to max_by(version) per id (mirroring meta-state), so the sidecar stores history but reads return the current state, not N stale copies.

GAP 2 — no way to stop/pause runtime tracking for a surface. Both writers (`runtime_state_record`, preflight-gated; `meta_state_dispatch_finding`, live-gated) append unconditionally — there is no per-surface tracking toggle, allowlist, or pause mechanism. When the operator is building the LOOP (not vnstock), vnstock's ledger-events still append (from vendored product code / hooks / earlier work) and pollute runtime-state.jsonl, mixing non-actionable vnstock noise with the loop's own meta-state-tools / runtime-state ledger-events that actually drive the self-learning loop. There is no MCP tool or config to say "stop tracking vnstock." Fix direction: a per-surface tracking gate — either (a) a tracked-surfaces allowlist / paused-surfaces denylist config that both writers consult before appending, or (b) a `runtime_state_pause`/`runtime_state_resume` MCP tool that flips a surface's tracking flag. Either keeps runtime-state.jsonl focused on the surfaces the operator actually runs.

Combined harm: the inbound gate's stale-observation scan and `runtime_state_read` both surface vnstock noise, eroding signal on the loop's own ledger-events; the sidecar grows monotonically with no dedup or stop. The two gaps compound — gap 2 keeps vnstock rows flowing in, gap 1 keeps every stale version of them.

Scope note: this is a template-repo concern — vnstock is the vendored example product; the operator is building the loop. The fix should make "I'm not running surface X" expressible and keep that surface's rows out of the loop's ledger view.

description: The write-capable CLI transport's context-savings dogfood check is ad-hoc, not systematized, and its results are not recorded in the loop's own ledger. During the review of commit ae431ef the savings were measured once by hand (31.8 KB of dropped MCP record-surface tool defs vs a 1.91 KB SessionStart banner = 29.9 KB / 94% saved per session start) using a throwaway script that was deleted after use. Three gaps: (1) no reproducible check — the measurement lives in no committed script, so it cannot re-run or track drift over time; (2) no runtime-state record — each measurement should be a runtime_state_record ledger-event (affected_system=runtime-state) so the loop's own ledger tracks context-size wins across sessions and surfaces regressions (a new MCP tool re-injected into context, or a sketch/banner re-bloat, would shrink the savings and be detectable from the ledger); (3) no regression guard tying the measurement to the existing <2 KiB banner budget lock (cli-sessionstart-banner.test.js) and the CLI_TOOLS drift guard. Systemize: a committed script (e.g. tools/scripts/measure-cli-context.mjs) or a vitest check that, for the current CLI_TOOLS set, computes dropped-def bytes vs banner bytes, asserts the banner stays under budget, and emits a runtime_state_record row per run. Upstream context: change-log entry meta-260722T1433Z (write-capable CLI landed) and resolved finding meta-260721T0809Z (transport diversification). This finding closes the dogfood-evidence loop by making the context savings measured-and-recorded, not asserted-once. No evidence_code_ref: the measurement system does not exist yet, so mechanism_check is false by default (gap finding, not a grounded one).

The drift test (cli-write-tool-set-drift.test.js) tags these MCP_RESIDUE entries with reason=deferred-rehoming per docs/runtime-contract.md L2 § Transport capability. L2 transport-capability criterion cited via change-log meta-260723T0811Z-docs-runtime-contract-md; this finding is the durable deferral record so the decision does not live only in the audit report. workflow_generate_prompt returned {error:true,message:Blueprint file not found} for EVERY call because its BLUEPRINTS map pointed at tools/learning-loop-mcp/references/*.md — a directory removed when the learning-loop-mcp package folded into learning-loop-mastra and references/ relocated under tools/handlers/ (commits 5788890 + b458f1b + 89fb6f2). The real files live at tools/learning-loop-mastra/tools/handlers/references/. The handler try/catch swallowed the ENOENT and returned a soft error, so the breakage was silent and untested (no test invoked workflow_generate_prompt with a real blueprint arg — only set-membership assertions existed). Fix: BLUEPRINTS repointed to the real location; regression test workflow-generate-prompt-tool.test.js pins that every blueprint category resolves a skeleton. Residual: the tool now works under the loop repo root but NOT under a non-loop runtime root (LOOP_READS_VIA_CLI=1 with GATE_ROOT=product repo) — the blueprints live in the loop package, so cross-root resolution (U-Q2) remains unresolved. workflow_generate_prompt is therefore reclassified CLI_READ_TOOLS -> MCP_RESIDUE deferred-rehoming (consistent with the portable-six finding meta-260723T0813Z) until a dedicated re-homing plan handles cross-root blueprint resolution. Discovered during the post-merge review of plan 260722-2147.

Aged findings (no verification.steps) cannot be re-grounded by meta_state_re_verify: the handler returns re_verified:false reason:no_verification_steps when entry.verification.steps is empty (meta-state-re-verify-tool.js:44-46), but 17 age-stale findings (e.g. meta-260614T1236Z-..., meta-260714T1248Z-...) are still grounded with hash_match:true — the operator has no canonical way to re-stamp last_verified_at without first authoring per-finding verification steps. Cold-tier test bumped its age-stale cap (11→19) as the documented operator escape hatch, but the cap is a regression-detection forcing function, not a real fix; the registry will continue to age until either (a) each aged finding gains verification.steps (large per-finding work) or (b) a lighter operator action (e.g. meta_state_touch) is added that stamps last_verified_at when checkGrounding passes.

The IMMUTABLE_PATCH_FIELDS deny-list in meta-state-patch-tool.js:6-23 blocks any attempt to clear `archived_at` / `archived_by` / `archived_reason` via meta_state_patch. In session 06085a38 (transcript line 465) the recovery from an erroneous rule archival required a direct Python edit of meta-state.jsonl, which bypassed the gate/audit surface, skipped the CAS path through updateEntry, and left `resolved_at`/`resolution` fields on the now-active entry. P0/P1 fixes for the same incident shipped (archive/resolve entry-kind guards, session_id discoverability, bulk-archive preview). The recommended remediation per plans/reports/debugger-260614-0207-session-06085a38-meta-state-process-gaps.md is either (a) extend meta_state_patch to allow archived -> active transitions and auto-clear archived_* fields, or (b) add a dedicated meta_state_unarchive tool. Direct JSONL edits must not remain a recovery path.

The runtime-agnostic pattern is real in this codebase (shim-not-fork, protocol-adapter, cross-surface iteration) but is NOT codified as a rule. The pattern exists in the code; what's missing is the codified invariant + the surfaces that teach it to future features and audit compliance.

Two existing asymmetries surface the gap:

1. tools/learning-loop-mcp/core/gate-logic.js:407 — GLOB_SCOPE_WHITELIST = ["product/", "docs/", "plans/", "tools/", ".factory/", "meta-state.jsonl"]. The list includes ".factory/" but NOT ".claude/". A future Claude-targeted glob pattern (e.g., a Claude-coordination equivalent of rule-project-skill-boundary) would be silently dropped by the whitelist check. This is a known asymmetry between the two supported runtimes.

2. tools/learning-loop-mcp/core/inbound-state.js:34-65 — readLastOperatorMessage hard-codes both .claude/coordination/ and .factory/coordination/ paths inline. The cross-surface iteration is duplicated logic; if a third surface is added, the function needs editing in two places (lines 45-54 + 59-69). Same anti-pattern recurs in the bash gate's PATH_WRITE_PATTERNS which lists ".claude/coordination/" and ".factory/coordination/" markers separately (tools/learning-loop-mcp/hooks/bash-gate.js:31-41).

The fix is the layered design captured in plans/reports/brainstorm-260615-1400-runtime-agnostic-features-rule.md. The design authors 6 implementation artifacts:

- AGENTS.md §2 amendment (the design spec; subsection "Runtime-Agnostic Pattern" + 6-item checklist)
- Meta-state rule entry rule-runtime-agnostic-features (the codified invariant; enforcement: agent, pattern_type: consult-checklist, pattern = JSON-serialized 6-item checklist)

Close-flow / finding-triage gap is the symptom; the root cause is architectural — the loop never promoted transport to L1. Transport is named in docs/runtime-contract.md (L2: the 4 transport-agnostic runtime capabilities, with MCP+hooks / library-import / shell-hook-only listed as candidate transports) and realized in docs/architecture.md (L3: the 3-layer architecture hard-codes MCP — "Runtime Interface" IS "the MCP-transport conformance checklist"), but the loop's core meta-state lifecycle operations (report / ack / log_change / resolve / refresh_file_index / dispatch / supersede) are implemented AS MCP tools (L3), not as Core functions (L1) behind a transport adapter. There is no L1 seam between "what the operation is" and "how it is invoked." MCP is de facto foundation because nothing above it abstracts the operation from the transport.

Two failure modes, both symptoms of the missing L1 seam:

(A) WRONG-ROOT MCP (alive but rooted at main): session f3972a8d-ba4e-48ea-a26d-f2152e5d3d99 worked in worktree .worktrees/fix-issue-34-fallow-self-verify/, but .mcp.json lives at the repo root and starts tools/learning-loop-mastra/mastra/server.js with LOOP_SURFACE=.claude rooted at main. The live MCP could not see worktree-only files: meta_state_refresh_file_index({path:"tools/learning-loop-mastra/scripts/gate-self-verify.mjs"}) returned code_missing even though the file existed in the worktree. The operation was unreachable because the operation IS the MCP tool — there is no Core function to call from a shell in the worktree.

(B) DEAD MCP (after pkill): the agent ran pkill -f "mastra/server.js" (exit 144) trying to re-root; every subsequent mcp__learning-loop__mastra_meta_state_* call returned "No such tool available." Restarting from the shell was blocked by the Claude Code auto-mode classifier as Self-Modification ("Starting/restarting the MCP server ... touches the agent's own MCP/runtime infrastructure"); a separate `git push origin main` for the close-flow commit was blocked as Git Push to Default Branch. The agent's own reasoning: "To restart it rooted at the worktree, I would need to change the .mcp.json or restart Claude Code." The only remaining path — the operator manually opening a fresh Claude Code session — is an out-of-band step with no in-loop mechanism.

Cornered-agent bypass attempts (defense-in-depth caught all): Write to file-index.jsonl blocked by the loop write-gate ("Direct writes ... poisoning the index would mask drift"); `node seed-file-index.mjs` blocked by the auto-classifier as Irreversible Local Destruction. These are the agent discovering, under pressure, that there is no non-MCP path to a core operation — a symptom of the missing L1 transport seam.

DEBATE TO OPEN (the unified plan must resolve this, not assume it; the debate spans BOTH surfaces): is MCP the correct transport for the learning loop's core state machine? MCP is an LLM-tool-calling protocol — agent-facing, stdio, a long-lived child process the agent cannot restart (classifier-blocked as self-modification) and cannot re-root to a worktree, and that dies when the shell dies. The loop's core operations are also operator-facing (close-flow after a merge), CI-facing (dispatch on PR event), and shell-facing (worktree work). Coupling audit-trail integrity to MCP couples it to a process with the wrong availability model for an audit trail. runtime-contract.md already names library-import and shell-hook-only transports as forward options; this finding argues they should be evaluated as peer first-class transports now, not deferred. The debate has two surfaces that must both be understood before deciding: (1) CONCEPTUAL (L1) — what transport means as an engine concept, the operation-vs-invocation seam, whether transport belongs in the engine invariant in docs/loop-engine.md, and what 'Core is transport-neutral' commits the loop to; (2) IMPLEMENTATION (L3) — how MCP / CLI / library each realize the 4 runtime capabilities, per-transport restart/re-root semantics, worktree rooting, and gate coverage (does the bash/write-gate see a CLI adapter the same way it sees an MCP tool call?). Promoting transport to L1 means: core meta-state operations are Core functions; a transport interface exposes them; MCP, CLI, and library are peer adapters. The CLI adapter is the immediate unblock (close-flow runs in the shell CWD, sees worktree state, survives MCP death). Whether MCP remains the default transport for audit-trail operations or becomes an agent-convenience adapter over a CLI/library primary is the debate — the evidence above (can't restart, can't re-root, dies with the shell) argues MCP should not be the load-bearing transport for audit-trail integrity.

Compounds with meta-260704T1010Z- (close-flow chat bullets are ephemeral): even with a live MCP, the close-flow contract is not enforced at meta_state_resolve time, so a cornered agent that skips steps leaves orphan findings and a degraded audit trail. The L1-transport promotion and the resolution-evidence gate are complementary: the gate enforces *what* the close-flow must produce; the transport layer determines *whether the agent can produce it*.

Resolution path (unified plan with meta-260704T1010Z-): (i) promote transport to L1 — define core meta-state operations as Core functions behind a transport interface; the doc-location decision (new docs/transport-layer.md vs extending docs/runtime-contract.md) is deferred to the plan and decided on AGENT READABILITY — whichever structure lets an agent locate 'the loop has N peer transports and Core is transport-neutral' in one read; (ii) ship a CLI adapter for log_change / resolve / refresh_file_index / dispatch that invokes Core directly, mirroring gate-self-verify.mjs — runs in the shell CWD, sees worktree state, survives MCP death (immediate unblock); (iii) make plans/reports/close-flow-*.md executable artifacts (Node script + registry-cited block) so `pnpm close-flow:run <finding-id>` works without MCP; (iv) gate meta_state_resolve behind a resolution-evidence-required rule requiring {pr_ref, change_log_id, file_index_refreshed_path}; (v) extend SessionStart stale_dispatch_hints to surface executable close-flow commands alongside open dispatches; (vi) decide the default transport for audit-trail operations (the debate — do not assume MCP stays default); (vii) decide worktree MCP rooting (per-worktree .mcp.json or a CWD-aware server) as a near-term mitigation while the debate is open. Acceptance: a close-flow executes end-to-end with node + shell only (no Claude Code session required); bash/write-gate covers all records/** and file-index.jsonl writes; every core meta-state operation is reachable through at least two transports.

Evidence anchor: evidence_code_ref is .mcp.json (the concrete wrong-root mechanism behind failure mode A, fingerprint-able). The L1 gap itself is an absence in docs/loop-engine.md and is not fingerprint-able; accepted — grounding checks track the symptom, the architectural gap is carried by this description.

Promoted regex rules in applyPromotedRules (gate-logic.js) were evaluated per-segment only: splitSegments splits a command on ; & | (honoring quotes), so no segment retained a literal pipe. A registry rule therefore could not match a cross-pipe pattern such as `vitest run ... 2>&1 | tail`, which made the State-3 backstop for raw-stdout parsing unexpressible as a promoted rule. Fixed by adding a full-command regex pass after the per-segment loop (safe strict superset: a pattern matching the full command either already matched a segment, or spans a removed delimiter — newly reachable; no active registry rule uses a literal `|`). The State-3 positive path is the `pnpm test:iter` wrapper; the promoted rule `rule-no-raw-stdout-vitest` is the deterministic backstop (operator to promote in live mode).

The canonical git union-merge driver command `git merge-file --union %O %A %B` is wrong — git merge-file writes its result to the first arg, so the result lands in %O (the ancestor copy), and git reads the unchanged %A (ours), silently dropping the other side. That is the exact data-loss merge=union exists to prevent. Corrected arg order: `git merge-file --union %A %O %B` (result lands in %A, ours, with %O as base and %B as other). Remediation: tools/scripts/setup-git-merge-drivers.sh sets the corrected driver per-clone, idempotent, with a wrong-order detection that refuses to silently overwrite (pass --force to acknowledge and overwrite). Documented in .gitattributes (comment) + AGENTS.md §8. .github/workflows/meta-state-refs-check.yml configures the driver on the ephemeral CI runner in a checkout step.

Branch-protection required-status-check satisfaction must be verified via the PR's mergeStateStatus (or commits/<sha>/check-runs[].name == required context), NOT via `gh pr view --json mergeable`. `mergeable` reports GitHub's merge-button state, which honors `enforce_admins:false` admin bypass — so an operator sees MERGEABLE regardless of whether required checks are actually satisfied, producing a false-positive completion claim. Concretely: a required check named after the Actions JOB id (`refs-check`) will never match a branch-protection context set to the workflow `name:` (`meta-state refs check`); the check stays PENDING while mergeable=MERGEABLE. Canonical mechanism: bind the required-check context to the parsed job id via `tools/scripts/setup-branch-protection.mjs` (single source of truth), and verify with `gh pr view <n> --json mergeStateStatus` == CLEAN. This finding reframes rule candidate `rule-required-status-checks-verify-combined-status` from the debug report at plans/reports/debug-cook-refs-check-context-mismatch-260715-1409-report.md.

(1) Schema: cross-ref fields declared per-kind in core/meta-state.js (promoted_to_rule at :317, plus consolidated_into, supersedes, addresses, proposed_design_for, reopens, origin). (2) Per-kind ref factories core/entry/{finding,rule,changelog,loop-design}.js each carry bespoke outboundRefs/inboundRefs; rule.js:68 documents 'Dual-field migration: rule.origin is the canonical promoted_to_rule ref' yet still scans finding.promoted_to_rule directly (rule.js:78) with a seenPromotedFrom dedup to avoid duplicate refs. (3) Inverse-index builder core/loop-introspect.js reconstructs promoted_to_rule_inverse from BOTH rule.origin (:616-623) AND finding.promoted_to_rule (:628). The consistency-check invariant set in core/consistency-check.js (META_STATE_CONSISTENCY_INVARIANTS) was authored under the pre-migration status enum (active/reported/resolved/superseded/archived/expired/auto-resolved). Remediation: audit each row against the new canonical enum, prune rows whose status is deleted, and re-anchor any constraint that needs to survive — e.g., the F-1 spirit ('open must not carry terminal audit fields') on status='open' with the forbid list drawn from the post-migration writeEntry contract. `meta_state_re_verify` is the lone operator-tier meta-state tool still using the inline `META_STATE_VERIFY_EXEC=1` env-var gate at `meta-state-re-verify-tool.js:29` — 5 sibling tools (`meta_state_supersede`, `meta_state_promote_rule`, `meta_state_ship_loop_design`, `meta_state_dispatch_finding`, `runtime_state_record`) have already migrated to `LOOP_SESSION_MODE=live` via `tools/lib/session-mode.js#isLiveSession`. The original 3-layer defense-in-depth design from `plans/260609-stale-flag-redesign/plan.md:142,206,218` locked in `(1) META_STATE_VERIFY_EXEC=1 env-gate; (2) cmd-allowlist from core/patterns.json#meta-state-verify-cmd-allowlist; (3) spawnSync with shell:false + 10s timeout`. Two questions sit in the gap between "preserved" and "migrated to canonical helper pattern":

(A) STAY SEPARATE from `LOOP_SESSION_MODE=live`. Verify is the only operator-tier tool that runs external processes — its threat surface (shell injection from registry-stored commands) is qualitatively different from "mutates registry" tools. description: The inter-finding relationship data model conflates three distinct mechanisms and the boundary between them is undocumented — causing a real conflation this session (two distinct findings share the meta-260716T2220Z timestamp; the `…redirect-split` finding's `reopens` edge was treated as a 'relationship' when the file-index was the right tool). Three mechanisms: (1a) 'findings related to a file' is already solved by `file-index.jsonl` (every finding with `evidence_code_ref` is grounded to its path; `check_grounding`/`refresh_file_index`/`query_drift` answer 'all findings on this file') — NOT a relationship edge; (1b) lifecycle lineage is carried by kind-pair-typed edges (`supersedes`, `consolidated_into`, `addresses`, `proposed_design_for`, `origin`) — keep; (2) 'solve one → resolve other' (cascade) is a closure POLICY (state transition) glued to the `reopens` edge via `cascade_from`, not a relationship type. Audit 2026-07-17: `reopens` set on 1/24 open findings (~4%, 1/102 total entries); the single parent `meta-260715T1328Z` was cascade-resolved (only observed cascade); the stale-status migration (plans 260611-1000, 260707-0812) already removed cascade's payoff — auto-closing a persisted-stale parent is no longer needed since 'open/deferred' is an acceptable resting state. Goals for the dedicated migration session: (a) STRENGTHEN (1a) — document the boundary explicitly in docs/meta-state-lifecycle.md + docs/architecture.md + a discoverability hint: file-index = 'findings on a file'; typed edges = lifecycle lineage; description prose = soft context; do NOT add a generic `related_to` field (DX trap: optional+vague → inconsistent → unqueryable); (b) MIGRATE (2) WITHOUT LOSING LINEAGE — drop `reopens` + `cascade_from` + `reopens_inverse` (core/loop-introspect.js:556,580,588,642-647,751) + the stale-guard in `meta_state_resolve`; on stale-succession, open a fresh finding and carry lineage as free-text in `description` (greppable, zero schema, zero orphan-ref risk); resolve parents by hand; add a closure-directive (`cascade_resolve:true`) as a SEPARATE concept layered on a relationship ONLY if a real recurrence cluster (>2 linked findings) appears (YAGNI). Migration safety (rule hint 7): import-chain analysis, not keyword-grep, before deleting; preserve ref-validation + canonical-compare. Lineage: this finding emerged from analyzing meta-260716T2220Z-agents-evade-rule-no-raw-stdout-vitest-by-a-two-command-redi (same debug session, adjacent); see plans/reports/debug-260716-2115-vitest-redirect-split-gate-evasion.md.

The rule-entry pattern field is validated as z.string() with no shape constraint for consult-checklist rules (tools/learning-loop-mastra/core/meta-state.js:281-282 and the meta_state_promote_rule tool schema at tools/handlers/meta-state-promote-rule-tool.js:21). consult-checklist patterns are JSON blobs of shape {version, items:[{id, description}]} (see rule-fallow-brief-on-gate-failure in meta-state.jsonl). Consumers JSON.parse(rule.pattern) at runtime — e.g. gate-logic-consult-checklist-tool-integration.test.js:82 and gate-logic-consult-checklist-fallow-brief.test.js:55, and any agent runtime that reads loop_describe rules. Because the schema permits any string, a malformed pattern (e.g. "[not-json") would be accepted at promotion time and only throw at the first JSON.parse. Fix: add a zod refinement on pattern for pattern_type==="consult-checklist" that validates JSON.parse-ability and the {version, items[]} shape, applied in both core/meta-state.js metaStateRuleEntrySchema and the promote-rule tool input schema. Surfaced in plans/reports/journal-260714-fallow-brief-discovery.md followup (b).

description: The consistency-check invariant set in core/consistency-check.js (META_STATE_CONSISTENCY_INVARIANTS) was authored under the pre-migration status enum (active/reported/resolved/superseded/archived/expired/auto-resolved). Plan 260707-0812 deleted status:active, status:reported, status:auto-resolved, status:expired; the canonical post-migration enum is now {open, resolved, superseded, archived}. The F-1 invariant row references the deleted status='active' — so the pure detector encodes an invariant that cannot fire on any live entry. The result is a probe that ships with silently-drifted invariants: F-2/F-3/F-4 still apply, NEW-1 (status='reported') is also dead. Remediation: audit each row against the new canonical enum, prune rows whose status is deleted, and re-anchor any constraint that needs to survive — e.g., the F-1 spirit ('open must not carry terminal audit fields') on status='open' with the forbid list drawn from the post-migration writeEntry contract. Source-of-truth for what audit fields 'open' can legitimately carry is the write-path invariants at tools/learning-loop-mastra/core/meta-state.js (resolve/supersede/archive handlers).
resolution: Remediated: F-1 re-anchored to status=open with forbid list drawn from resolve/supersede/archive handlers in core/meta-state.js (resolved_at, resolved_by, resolution, consolidated_into, superseded_at, archived_at, archived_by, archived_reason); dead NEW-1 row (status=reported) pruned. Invariant set is now F-1..F-4, all keyed on the post-migration enum. Tests updated: C-9/C-10 cover supersede/archive markers on open, C-16 asserts 4 invariants; 24/24 consistency-check tests pass.

pattern: {"version": 1, "items": [{"id": "read-required-contexts", "description": "Read the branch-protection required_status_checks via `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/branches/<branch>/protection/required_status_checks` and note the required `context` string(s)."}, {"id": "match-check-run-name", "description": "Confirm via `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/commits/<sha>/check-runs` that a check run whose `name` equals a required `context` exists with conclusion \"success\"; GitHub matches required checks against the check-run NAME, which for Actions is the JOB id, not the workflow `name:` field."}, {"id": "verify-combined-status", "description": "Confirm satisfaction via `gh pr view <n> --json mergeStateStatus` == \"CLEAN\" (or the combined commit status), NOT via `gh pr view --json mergeable` \u2014 `mergeable` reports the merge-button state, honors enforce_admins:false admin bypass, and is a false-positive completion claim here."}, {"id": "bind-context-to-job-id", "description": "If the required context and the check-run name differ, bind the context to the job id via `tools/scripts/setup-branch-protection.mjs` (single source of truth) before claiming done."}]}
description: Gate-enforced rule: rule-required-status-checks-verify-combined-status. Pattern type=agent-checklist; pattern is the canonical JSON checklist (version 1, 4 items) of required-status-check verification steps.
hint_text: Required-status-check satisfaction verification. Before claiming a GitHub branch-protection required status check is satisfied, verify via `gh pr view <n> --json mergeStateStatus` == CLEAN (or `commits/<sha>/check-runs[].name` equals a required `context` with `conclusion: success`), NOT via `gh pr view --json mergeable` — `mergeable` reports the merge-button state and honors `enforce_admins:false` admin bypass, so it returns MERGEABLE regardless of required-check state (a false-positive completion claim). GitHub matches a required context against the check-run NAME, which for Actions is the JOB id, NOT the workflow `name:` field; if they differ, bind the context to the job id via `tools/scripts/setup-branch-protection.mjs` before claiming done. See `rule-required-status-checks-verify-combined-status` in `meta-state.jsonl` for the full contract.

description: No MCP tool exists to invalidate the running MCP server's ESM module cache. The server caches imports at startup, so edits to core/loop-introspect.js (PROCESS_HINTS) mid-session do not surface in loop_describe({tier: warm}).process_hints until the server restarts (journal-260714-fallow-brief-discovery.md lesson 4). Plan assertions about warm-tier live state are therefore confined to "process_hints count went up by 1" sanity checks, not full validation; the H6 ordering gate fires as a transient warning for any rule promoted before its PROCESS_HINTS row is visible to the running runtime. Proposal: expose a cache_invalidate MCP tool that re-imports (or clears the cache for) named core modules so future plans can refresh module caches without a server restart. Until it lands, the cold-session parity test (readFileSync-based) remains the source-of-truth validator. Surfaced in plans/reports/journal-260714-fallow-brief-discovery.md followup (d).
resolution: Structurally closed by CLI migration instead of a cache_invalidate tool. The original gap was a long-running MCP server caching ESM imports so mid-session PROCESS_HINTS edits did not surface until restart. All three wired runtimes (.claude, .factory, .mastracode) now set LOOP_RECORDS_VIA_CLI=1, moving the full record surface (reads + writes, including loop_describe warm tier) onto the stateless bin/loop.mjs CLI — every invocation is a fresh process with fresh module imports, so no runtime retains a server-lifetime ESM cache over the record surface and the staleness mechanism cannot manifest. The MCP server keeps only the workflow/storage/allowlist/audit residue. Pinned by mcp-config.test.js EXPECTED_ENV; change-log meta-260725T2335Z-factory-mcp-json-mastracode-mcp-json-env.

description:
Promoting an agent-checklist rule is a manual 4-location cascade with no automated coupling, and 3 of those locations hardcode registry counts that are trivially derivable. This just caused the PR-#73 CI failure (rule-no-plan-ids-in-stable-code-artifacts).

The 4 locations an agent-checklist rule promotion MUST touch:
1. `meta-state.jsonl` — the rule entry (id, enforcement, pattern_type=agent-checklist, pattern, hint_text). Done by `meta_state_promote_rule` MCP tool. This is the ONLY location the tool writes.
2. `core/hint-registry.js` — a hand-mirrored `HINT_REGISTRY` entry with `derived_from_rule === rule.id`, a slug, `kind: "process"`, `text: ""` (renderer resolves prose from `rule.hint_text`), and a one-line `suggestion`. The promote tool CANNOT write this (it writes the registry, not source code). Missing it fails `legacy-mcp/consult-checklist-process-hints-coverage.test.js` (the Phase-3 invariant: every active agent-checklist rule MUST have a matching `derived_from_rule` registry entry). This is the failure that broke CI.
3. `__tests__/hint-registry.test.cjs` — hardcodes `process` slug count (10), `buildProcessHints` length (10), `listHints({kind:'process'})` length (10), and total (26).
4. `__tests__/hint-renderer.test.cjs` + `__tests__/rule-derived-process-hints.test.cjs` — hardcode total hints (26), degraded-skip warnings count (8), sidecar `process_hints` length (10), mcp-warm array length (26), provenance rows (26), and "8 rule-derived process rows at positions 2-10".

Root smell: the numeric counts (26/10/8) are PURE DERIVATIONS of `HINT_REGISTRY.length`, `.filter(e => e.derived_from_rule).length`, and `.filter(e => e.kind === 'process').length` — yet they are hand-locked as literals. Adding one rule-derived hint bumps 26->27, 10->11, 8->9 and requires hand-editing all 3 test files. The agent must know to do this; nothing enforces or reminds them. The slug-list + ordering assertions in these tests ARE legitimate (they catch real drift) and should stay hardcoded — only the pure-numeric counts should be derived.

Two coupled gaps:
A. The promote tool does not (cannot) create the companion `HINT_REGISTRY` entry — the agent must hand-edit `core/hint-registry.js`. No reminder, no checklist hint (ironically, the rule-promotion workflow itself lacks the agent-checklist treatment).
B. The count-locking tests hardcode derivable numbers, turning a 1-location registry addition into a 4-file manual cascade.

Remediation direction:
- Gap A: either (i) a companion `register_hint_for_rule` MCP tool (or a `meta_state_promote_rule` option) that appends the `HINT_REGISTRY` entry to `core/hint-registry.js` from the rule id + hint_text (slug = rule-id minus 'rule-' prefix; suggestion = first sentence of hint_text; derived_from_rule = rule.id), so promotion is 1 MCP call; or (ii) an agent-checklist rule + regression test that forbids an active agent-checklist rule without a `HINT_REGISTRY` entry (the coverage test already does this — so the real fix is making the promote path produce the entry, not just flag its absence).
- Gap B: replace the hardcoded numeric counts in the 3 test files with `HINT_REGISTRY`-derived values (`registry.HINT_REGISTRY.length`, `.filter(derived_from_rule).length`, `.filter(kind==='process').length`). Keep the slug-list + ordering + per-partition-budget assertions hardcoded (those are the real signal). After this, adding a rule-derived hint is: 1 promote call + 1 slug-list append (the legitimate drift signal) — not a 4-file cascade.

Evidence: the PR-#73 CI failure (run 29849986465, `test` workflow) was exactly gap A (missing HINT_REGISTRY entry); the 9 follow-on test failures from the fix were exactly gap B (hardcoded counts). Both gaps are reproducible by promoting any new agent-checklist rule.
resolution: Plan 260726-0029 retired the hand-mirror: rule-derived process hints are now generated by buildProcessView({rulesById}) from active agent-checklist rules (core/hint-registry.js). The 9 hand-mirrored HINT_REGISTRY rows are deleted; promoting a rule is a single meta_state_promote_rule CLI call carrying hint_text + hint_suggestion (the buildProcessView reads both unconditionally). Coverage test inverts to assert rule→view presence + hint_text+hint_suggestion presence + slug uniqueness. Test count literals are derived from the view; only slug lists / merged-order / partition-budget assertions stay hardcoded (the legitimate drift signal). Slug-collision guard (Phase 1) rejects promote/patch of a derived slug that collides with a standalone or another active rule.

description:
`meta_state_re_verify` is the lone operator-tier meta-state tool still using the inline `META_STATE_VERIFY_EXEC=1` env-var gate at `meta-state-re-verify-tool.js:29` — 5 sibling tools (`meta_state_supersede`, `meta_state_promote_rule`, `meta_state_ship_loop_design`, `meta_state_dispatch_finding`, `runtime_state_record`) have already migrated to `LOOP_SESSION_MODE=live` via `tools/lib/session-mode.js#isLiveSession`. The original 3-layer defense-in-depth design from `plans/260609-stale-flag-redesign/plan.md:142,206,218` locked in `(1) META_STATE_VERIFY_EXEC=1 env-gate; (2) cmd-allowlist from core/patterns.json#meta-state-verify-cmd-allowlist; (3) spawnSync with shell:false + 10s timeout`. The 260707 rework (`plans/260707-0812-.../phase-03:46,55`) re-affirmed: "`META_STATE_VERIFY_EXEC` gate preserved." Two questions sit in the gap between "preserved" and "migrated to canonical helper pattern":

(A) STAY SEPARATE from `LOOP_SESSION_MODE=live`. Verify is the only operator-tier tool that runs external processes — its threat surface (shell injection from registry-stored commands) is qualitatively different from "mutates registry" tools. Merging collapses Layer 1 (the process-level kill-switch), breaks CI/test isolation (`OPERATOR_MODE=1` is set for fixture writes without enabling exec), and creates a foot-gun. The defense-in-depth is load-bearing, not vestigial.

(B) MIGRATE to the canonical `#lib/*-mode.js` helper pattern. Extract `tools/lib/exec-mode.js` mirroring `session-mode.js` (exports `isExecSession()` returning `process.env.META_STATE_VERIFY_EXEC === "1"`); refactor `meta-state-re-verify-tool.js:29` to call it. Extend `session-mode.js` JSDoc with a sibling-pointer: "session-mode authorizes operator-tier mutations; exec-mode authorizes running registry-stored commands." Fills red-team gap C3 from `plans/260626-0607-phase-e-housekeeping/reports/general-purpose-260626-0616-...` ("Plan does not document how to set `META_STATE_VERIFY_EXEC=1` in the MCP server's environment").

Resolution path: (i) ship `tools/lib/exec-mode.js#isExecSession` (zero behavior change); (ii) refactor `meta-state-re-verify-tool.js:29` to call it; (iii) extend `session-mode.js` JSDoc with sibling-pointer; (iv) decision on `.mcp.json`: add `META_STATE_VERIFY_EXEC=1` env if operator wants re_verify to actually run registry-stored steps in this session, or leave unset + use operator-audited `meta_state_patch` direct stamp (precedent: `plans/260626-0607-phase-e-housekeeping/phase-05-i2-re-verify-entry-9.md:201-204`). Acceptance: re_verify behavior unchanged; implementation surface aligns with sibling tools; `.mcp.json` env field becomes documented.

Operational symptom: in this Claude Code session `meta_state_re_verify` returns `verify_exec_required` because `.mcp.json` boots with only `LOOP_SURFACE=.claude`; `META_STATE_VERIFY_EXEC` is unset. Operator-audited patch path (via `meta_state_patch` direct `last_verified_at` write) is the documented workaround for entries without `verification.steps`. Compounds with `meta-260717T1101Z-the-consistency-check-invariant-set-in-core-consistency-chec` — both surface meta-state tool implementations drifting from canonical helper patterns; together they justify a "tool-grammar-consistency" audit (possible rule-promotion candidate).
resolution: Decision B implemented (operator decision 2026-07-26): extracted the inline META_STATE_VERIFY_EXEC check into tools/lib/exec-mode.js#isExecSession (fail-closed, accepts 1|true), refactored meta-state-re-verify-tool.js to call the helper, and extended session-mode.js JSDoc with the sibling-pointer. Behavior unchanged (17/17 tests pass: exec-mode 4, session-mode 8, re-verify 5). .mcp.json env left unset — meta_state_touch is the operator path for steps-empty findings since the patch direct-stamp workaround is deny-listed. The exec gate stays independent of LOOP_SESSION_MODE on purpose: re_verify is the sole tool spawning registry-stored commands. description: Universal-hooks unification is half-shipped. tools/learning-loop-mastra/hooks/universal/ holds 6 canonical hook implementations (bash-gate, inbound-gate, write-gate, recurrence-check-on-start, session-start-inject-discoverability, session-start-inject-process-hints), but adoption is per-runtime and ad hoc: .claude wires only the two session-start hooks from universal/ via settings.json (its bash/write/inbound/recurrence hooks instead point at .claude/coordination/hooks/*.cjs, a separate parallel tree); .factory wires none of universal/ — it uses .factory/coordination/hooks/* plus its own SessionStart adapter .factory/hooks/loop-surface-inject.cjs (single-source content but runtime-local wiring, per plans/260717-1826-unify-context-injection); .mastracode has recurrence-check only, no hint injection (pull-only by decision). Skills got a central mechanism (canonical source + pnpm skills:sync fan-out + skills-lock.json manifest + parity tests, plans/260719-1428); hooks got none — plans/260719-1428-central-skills-management/plan.md:20 explicitly deferred hooks/coordination centralization, and no follow-up plan exists. Consequences: (1) no manifest declares which hooks each runtime SHOULD wire, so drift is invisible — there is no equivalent of skills-mirror-parity.test.js for hooks; (2) 3 of the 6 universal hooks are wired by zero runtimes, i.e. dead canonical code or un-adopted capability (unclear which); (3) new hooks added to universal/ have no defined adoption path. Scope decision needed: either define a hooks manifest + per-runtime wiring matrix with a parity test (skills-model), or explicitly bless the current per-runtime wiring and delete/relocate unwired universal hooks. Evidence: .claude/settings.json:2-46 vs .factory/settings.json:2-38 vs .factory/hooks.json:8; tools/scripts/sync-skills.mjs header (skills-only scope).

Universal-hooks unification is half-shipped: three coexisting adoption patterns with no manifest declaring which hooks each runtime SHOULD wire. Pattern A (direct wiring): .claude/settings.json calls tools/learning-loop-mastra/hooks/universal/session-start-inject-{discoverability,process-hints}.cjs in place — no shim. Pattern B (shim): the 4 gate hooks (bash/write/inbound/recurrence) ship as byte-identical shims at {.claude,.factory,.mastracode}/coordination/hooks/*.cjs that exec universal/*.js; byte-identity is enforced by the shims-in-sync checklist item (core/runtime-agnostic-checklist.js). Pattern C (runtime-local adapter): .factory/hooks/loop-surface-inject.cjs — Droid-only SessionStart adapter, single-source content via direct core import (plans/260717-1826) but runtime-local wiring; NOT a shim, NOT covered by shims-in-sync, and NOT in CHANGE_LOG_BOUND_PATHS (see meta-260714T1248Z-change-log-bound-paths-tools-learning-loop-mastra-core-chang). Skills by contrast have one declared mechanism: canonical source + skills-lock.json manifest + pnpm skills:sync fan-out + skills-mirror-parity.test.js (plans/260719-1428; that plan explicitly deferred hooks centralization at plan.md:20, and no follow-up plan exists). Consequences: (1) shim byte-identity is checked but wiring coverage is not — nothing verifies each runtime's settings.json/hooks.json wires the full expected hook set, so a runtime silently losing a hook (or a new universal hook never getting adopted) is invisible; (2) why session-start hooks use Pattern A while gate hooks use Pattern B is undocumented — a new hook has no defined adoption path; (3) Pattern C is a detection blind spot on two axes (parity + change-log). Scope decision: define a hooks manifest + per-runtime wiring matrix with a parity test (skills-model), or document the 3-pattern split as intentional and add a wiring-coverage test only. Evidence: .claude/settings.json:2-46, .factory/settings.json:2-38, .factory/hooks.json:8, .mastracode/coordination/hooks/, core/runtime-agnostic-checklist.js.

CHANGE_LOG_BOUND_PATHS (tools/learning-loop-mastra/core/change-log-bound-paths.js:41-52) omits the runtime-surface hooks mirrors (.factory/hooks/**, .claude/hooks/**, .mastracode/hooks/**). The cold-session parity test enforces byte-for-byte equality between core/loop-introspect.js PROCESS_HINTS and .factory/hooks/loop-surface-inject.cjs LOCAL_PROCESS_HINTS (cold-session-discoverability.test.cjs:314), so .factory/hooks/loop-surface-inject.cjs is a real source-of-truth surface that gets edited. Yet Rec 12 gap-detection (isBoundPath) ignores drift on this path: editing the hook mirror without a change-log entry is not flagged as a gap. The detection set has skills mirrors for all three surfaces but no hooks mirrors for any of them. Scope decision needed: add only .factory/hooks/** (the surface actually in use) or all three runtime-surface hooks mirrors for symmetry with the skills entries. Note change-log-bound-paths.test.js:39-59 pins coverage via .includes() (not exact-equality), so adding entries will not break the existing test. Surfaced in plans/reports/journal-260714-fallow-brief-discovery.md followup (a).
resolution: Fixed: .factory/hooks/** added to CHANGE_LOG_BOUND_PATHS (core/change-log-bound-paths.js). Scope decision resolved: only .factory has a hooks/ tree (.claude/hooks, .mastracode/hooks do not exist; coordination/hooks/*.cjs gate shims are a separate mirrored tree), so a single entry binds the sole runtime hooks adapter. The byte-parity premise in the original description was retired by the single-source SessionStart refactor (LOCAL_PROCESS_HINTS deleted), but the adapter remains hand-edited code — the detection gap was real and is now closed. description: The write-capable CLI transport's context-savings dogfood check is ad-hoc, not systematized, and its results are not recorded in the loop's own ledger. During the review of commit ae431ef the savings were measured once by hand (31.8 KB of dropped MCP record-surface tool defs vs a 1.91 KB SessionStart banner = 29.9 KB / 94% saved per session start) using a throwaway script that was deleted after use. Three gaps: (1) no reproducible check — the measurement lives in no committed script, so it cannot re-run or track drift over time; (2) no runtime-state record — each measurement should be a runtime_state_record ledger-event (affected_system=runtime-state) so the loop's own ledger tracks context-size wins across sessions and surfaces regressions (a new MCP tool re-injected into context, or a sketch/banner re-bloat, would shrink the savings and be detectable from the ledger); (3) no regression guard tying the measurement to the existing <2 KiB banner budget lock (cli-sessionstart-banner.test.js) and the CLI_TOOLS drift guard. Systemize: a committed script (e.g. tools/scripts/measure-cli-context.mjs) or a vitest check that, for the current CLI_TOOLS set, computes dropped-def bytes vs banner bytes, asserts the banner stays under budget, and emits a runtime_state_record row per run. Upstream context: change-log entry meta-260722T1433Z (write-capable CLI landed) and resolved finding meta-260721T0809Z (transport diversification). This finding closes the dogfood-evidence loop by making the context savings measured-and-recorded, not asserted-once. No evidence_code_ref: the measurement system does not exist yet, so mechanism_check is false by default (gap finding, not a grounded one).
resolution: systematized via plans/260726-1953-cli-context-savings-measurement-and-ledger-dogfood. Phase 2: tools/scripts/measure-cli-context.mjs (pnpm measure:context) prints the delta JSON, --record mints the runtime-state preflight marker and writes a verifiable ledger row whose evidence_code_ref is the live measurement script. Recorded row id visible via runtime_state_read (verified post-run).

description: The canonical git union-merge driver command `git merge-file --union %O %A %B` is wrong — git merge-file writes its result to the first arg, so the result lands in %O (the ancestor copy), and git reads the unchanged %A (ours), silently dropping the other side. That is the exact data-loss merge=union exists to prevent. Corrected arg order: `git merge-file --union %A %O %B` (result lands in %A, ours, with %O as base and %B as other). Remediation: tools/scripts/setup-git-merge-drivers.sh sets the corrected driver per-clone, idempotent, with a wrong-order detection that refuses to silently overwrite (pass --force to acknowledge and overwrite). Documented in .gitattributes (comment) + AGENTS.md §8. .github/workflows/meta-state-refs-check.yml configures the driver on the ephemeral CI runner in a checkout step.
resolution: Resolved: corrected arg order is shipped and verified against live state. Live clone `git config --get merge.union.driver` = `git merge-file --union %A %O %B` (correct — result lands in %A/ours, %O base, %B other; the wrong `%O %A %B` would land the result in the ancestor and silently drop theirs). .gitattributes documents the corrected order + data-loss rationale. tools/scripts/setup-git-merge-drivers.sh ships the canonical value with wrong-order detection that refuses to silently overwrite (--force to acknowledge). .github/workflows/meta-state-refs-check.yml configures the driver on the ephemeral CI runner with the corrected order (Phase 4 F13). AGENTS.md §8 documents the one-time per-clone setup. No code change needed — remediation already in place; closing as verified.

description: Branch-protection required-status-check satisfaction must be verified via the PR's mergeStateStatus (or commits/<sha>/check-runs[].name == required context), NOT via `gh pr view --json mergeable`. `mergeable` reports GitHub's merge-button state, which honors `enforce_admins:false` admin bypass — so an operator sees MERGEABLE regardless of whether required checks are actually satisfied, producing a false-positive completion claim. Concretely: a required check named after the Actions JOB id (`refs-check`) will never match a branch-protection context set to the workflow `name:` (`meta-state refs check`); the check stays PENDING while mergeable=MERGEABLE. Canonical mechanism: bind the required-check context to the parsed job id via `tools/scripts/setup-branch-protection.mjs` (single source of truth), and verify with `gh pr view <n> --json mergeStateStatus` == CLEAN. This finding reframes rule candidate `rule-required-status-checks-verify-combined-status` from the debug report at plans/reports/debug-cook-refs-check-context-mismatch-260715-1409-report.md.
resolution: Resolved: required-check context is bound to the Actions JOB id and verified live. `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/branches/main/protection` returns checks:[{context:"refs-check"}], contexts:["refs-check"], strict:true — the required context is the job id `refs-check`, NOT the workflow display name `meta-state refs check`, so the check no longer stays PENDING behind an admin bypass. tools/scripts/setup-branch-protection.mjs is the single source of truth (parses job id from workflow YAML, writes it into protection, verifies after PUT). .github/workflows/meta-state-refs-check.yml documents the invariant. Rule rule-required-status-checks-verify-combined-status is active (v3, origin=this finding) carrying the agent-checklist enforcement (read required contexts, match check-run name, verify via mergeStateStatus==CLEAN not mergeable, bind context to job id). No code change needed — remediation shipped and rule promoted; closing as verified.
