This is the echo/printf prose false-positive class (the locked echo limitation, gate-logic-data-command-quotes.test.js:88), distinct from meta-260807T1347Z (loop.mjs CLI inline JSON argv) which is resolved by stripCliArgvPayload in plan 260807-1401-bash-gate-cli-argv-payload-strip. Stays open: resolving requires relaxing the echo/printf prose limitation with pipe-target-aware threat modeling (the echo X | bash bypass), deferred to a follow-up plan.

Shape recovered definitively 2026-08-07 from the originating session transcript (session 32a5ef87-f7bd-402e-99fa-fb40e24c9050): all 3 events are `printf '%s\n' '<json tool_input>' | node tools/learning-loop-mastra/hooks/universal/bash-gate.js; echo "---exit=$?---"` — the agent feeding a hook payload into the gate on stdin. The decision-log command_prefix truncates at ~120 chars and the recurrence_key hashes only the first 50 chars (normalizePrefix/COMMAND_PREFIX_MAX_LEN), so neither stored surface could reveal the tail; the transcript could. The trailing `| node` is a REAL pipe, NOT a redirect. The per-segment echo/printf prose relaxation (stripEchoProseSafe) deliberately preserves prose on ANY real pipe regardless of target, because classifying pipe targets as inert-vs-executing is unsound (tee/dd/cat persist; the exec-sink tail is unbounded) and rule-no-raw-stdout-vitest has NO matchConstraintPattern backstop. These 3 events therefore still escalate — verified empirically: actual command -> escalate; same payload with the trailing pipe removed -> ok. STAYS OPEN: this is a residual false positive whose only known fix is pipe-target classification, which was rejected as unsound. The prose class itself IS fixed for no-redirect/no-pipe shapes (see the echo-prose pipe-target regression suite). Do not archive: archiving re-admits the recurrence_key and the append-only decision-log entries would re-file at next SessionStart.

Pre-existing (NOT introduced by the echo-prose relaxation): promoted-rule regexes are matched against raw shell text, so adjacent-quote concatenation hides a banned token. `echo "widgetctl"" run evil" | bash` returns ok because the raw segment text reads `widgetctl"" run` and the rule's `\s+` cannot match the embedded quote chars, even though the shell concatenates the two quoted strings into `widgetctl run evil` and pipes it to bash. Verified identical on HEAD and on the relaxation branch (old=ok, new=ok), so this is orthogonal to that change. Same class applies to any rule whose pattern spans a token boundary an author can split with quotes (also reachable via `w''idgetctl run`, `$'wid'getctl`). Fix direction if pursued: normalize quote-concatenation (drop empty quoted regions and join adjacent quoted runs) before regex matching, in the same layer as the existing blank* helpers — NOT by loosening the rule patterns. Discovered while adversarially probing the per-segment echo/printf prose relaxation.

Pre-existing (NOT introduced by the echo-prose relaxation): promoted-rule regexes match raw shell text, so a banned token composed from pieces is never seen. Verified identical on HEAD and on the relaxation branch, so this is orthogonal to that change. Three confirmed shapes, one root cause. (1) Adjacent-quote concatenation: echo "widgetctl"" run evil" piped to bash returns ok, because the raw text reads widgetctl"" run and the rule's whitespace class cannot cross the quote chars, though the shell concatenates to widgetctl run evil and pipes it to bash. (2) Format/argument split: printf -v x with the pipe half in the format string and the verb half in the argument returns ok, because the two operands only become contiguous after printf formats them. (3) Cross-segment variable composition: printf -v x holding the verb half, then a sibling segment appending the pipe half inside the expansion, returns ok, because the halves live in different segments and are joined only by shell expansion at run time. Same family as any w''idgetctl run or $'wid'getctl construction. Fix direction if pursued: a normalization layer alongside the existing blank* helpers that folds quote-concatenation before matching; full dataflow through shell variables is out of reach for a regex gate and should be acknowledged as a bounded limitation rather than chased. Discovered while adversarially probing the per-segment echo/printf prose relaxation; the printf -v shapes were surfaced by a code-review subagent.

Gate-verb allowance discovery tax: every session that hits an executor verb (bash/eval/node -e) re-derives the 30-min gate-verb observation incantation from scratch. In session 126e391e (ak-ship of PR 120) recording one gate-verb:bash observation took 15 bash calls and ~2 min wall-clock: a proactive meta_state_list check, a registry grep, a failed gate_mark_preflight with bare-key JSON ({surface:...} rejected, retried with {"surface":...} after a --schema detour), 4 grep/find commands hunting the source_ref meta-state id, runtime_state_record --schema paged twice to learn required fields, and finally the record. The session ran uncached throughout (cache_read=0 on all 195 turns, 16.4M input tokens total), so the ~15 discovery turns re-read ~55-65k context each (~0.9M input tokens) to emit one runtime-state row. Root cause: evaluate-bash-gate.js emits a non-self-remediating block reason ('Constraint gate-verb:bash detected. No active observation found. Record an observation before proceeding.') that names the disease but not the cure — no incantation, no id==affected_system rule, no source_ref format. Compounded by: (1) no loop_get_instruction key for gate-verb-allowance (Unknown hint key), so the only guidance is the dense CLAUDE.md prose paragraph; (2) CLI rejects bare-key JSON with a bare exit 2 and no fix hint; (3) source_ref requires a meta-state finding id the agent must grep meta-state.jsonl to discover; (4) the gate_mark_preflight -> runtime_state_record two-tool protocol ordering is non-obvious. The gate already knows the blocked verb, the required tool, the required fields, and the id==affected_system rule at block time — it just does not emit them. Fix direction: self-remediating block message emitting the exact two-call incantation with the verb substituted and a fresh timestamp, plus a sentinel source_ref (local:meta-state:gate-verb-allowance) so the agent never greps for a finding id. Distinct from open finding meta-260807T1754Z (which captures the test-runner block, not the discovery cost).

description: The inter-finding relationship data model conflates three distinct mechanisms and the boundary between them is undocumented — causing a real conflation this session (two distinct findings share the meta-260716T2220Z timestamp; the `…redirect-split` finding's `reopens` edge was treated as a 'relationship' when the file-index was the right tool). Three mechanisms: (1a) 'findings related to a file' is already solved by `file-index.jsonl` (every finding with `evidence_code_ref` is grounded to its path; `check_grounding`/`refresh_file_index`/`query_drift` answer 'all findings on this file') — NOT a relationship edge; (1b) lifecycle lineage is carried by kind-pair-typed edges (`supersedes`, `consolidated_into`, `addresses`, `proposed_design_for`, `origin`) — keep; (2) 'solve one → resolve other' (cascade) is a closure POLICY (state transition) glued to the `reopens` edge via `cascade_from`, not a relationship type. Audit 2026-07-17: `reopens` set on 1/24 open findings (~4%, 1/102 total entries); the single parent `meta-260715T1328Z` was cascade-resolved (only observed cascade); the stale-status migration (plans 260611-1000, 260707-0812) already removed cascade's payoff — auto-closing a persisted-stale parent is no longer needed since 'open/deferred' is an acceptable resting state. Goals for the dedicated migration session: (a) STRENGTHEN (1a) — document the boundary explicitly in docs/meta-state-lifecycle.md + docs/architecture.md + a discoverability hint: file-index = 'findings on a file'; typed edges = lifecycle lineage; description prose = soft context; do NOT add a generic `related_to` field (DX trap: optional+vague → inconsistent → unqueryable); (b) MIGRATE (2) WITHOUT LOSING LINEAGE — drop `reopens` + `cascade_from` + `reopens_inverse` (core/loop-introspect.js:556,580,588,642-647,751) + the stale-guard in `meta_state_resolve`; on stale-succession, open a fresh finding and carry lineage as free-text in `description` (greppable, zero schema, zero orphan-ref risk); resolve parents by hand; add a closure-directive (`cascade_resolve:true`) as a SEPARATE concept layered on a relationship ONLY if a real recurrence cluster (>2 linked findings) appears (YAGNI). Migration safety (rule hint 7): import-chain analysis, not keyword-grep, before deleting; preserve ref-validation + canonical-compare. Lineage: this finding emerged from analyzing meta-260716T2220Z-agents-evade-rule-no-raw-stdout-vitest-by-a-two-command-redi (same debug session, adjacent); see plans/reports/debug-260716-2115-vitest-redirect-split-gate-evasion.md. Audit 2026-08-09 (new event): `meta_state_supersede` on two pre-normalization storm duplicates (`meta-202608030808391Z-c25c0e36`, `meta-202608030923447Z-2f734aa1`) created `consolidated_into` citation edges into change-log `meta-260809T1735Z-gate-logic-stripheredocbodies-recurrence-key-normalization` (citation rows `citation-mslriodz-xig8rl` / `citation-mslriowe-7q00e9`), yet `meta_state_relationships({id, direction:'both'})` returns `outbound:null` for both superseded findings — the `consolidated_into` lineage edge (mechanism 1b) is persisted in storage but NOT projected by the relationship-query surface. Directly confirms the boundary this finding flags: lifecycle lineage lives in storage yet is invisible to the relationships tool, so 'is there a lineage edge?' and 'what does relationships return?' diverge. Strengthens goal (a): the docs/discoverability hint should also state WHICH surface projects WHICH edge kind (today `relationships` surfaces kind-pair typed edges but not `consolidated_into`; the citation row is the only projection of a supersede).
